approval.cost: No fee for creating an OAuth2 application or distributing an integration is stated anywhere in the docs read
approval.trigger: No app review or approval gate is documented. Nothing in the Inbox API documentation describes a review, submission, or approval step before external users can authorize your OAuth2 application. The developer home page's 'Building a Public Integration' guidance is: 'Will you be marketing your project to the public? Awesome! But before you launch anything, please read over our brand guidelines to make sure everything looks tip top. When it's finished, be sure to let us know so we can tell everyone about it.' Public distribution is a notify-us/brand-guidelines arrangement, not an approval process. No marketplace listing process, submission form, or review timeline is described, and no pre-approval user/install caps are stated.

blockers.detail: 'All credentials must be associated with an active, invited user in the Help Scout account; a 401 error will be returned if a user does not meet these credentials.' A deactivated or uninvited user behind a connection silently breaks it.
blockers.howToClear: Monitor for 401s per connection and be ready to have the customer re-authorize with an active user.
blockers.title: User-status dependency

blockers.detail: 'Expect that the length of all access token types will change over time... they will grow and shrink over time. Please use a variable length data type without a specific maximum size to store access or refresh tokens.' Fixed-length token columns are an explicit trap. Refreshing also returns a new access AND refresh token pair, so a stored old refresh token must be replaced on every refresh.
blockers.howToClear: Store tokens in unbounded-length fields and persist the replacement pair atomically.
blockers.title: Token storage traps

flavor.recommended: An OAuth2 application using the Authorization Code flow
flavor.why: The object is an OAuth2 application created inside a Help Scout account under Your Profile > My apps > Create My App, yielding an application ID (client_id) and application secret (client_secret). It serves the Inbox API (formerly Mailbox API v2). 'The Authorization Code flow is typically used for integrations to be used by other Help Scout users': each customer authorizes your one application and you receive a per-customer access/refresh token pair. No scopes are documented on the Authentication page: the authorize URL shown takes only client_id and state.

humanMust: Create the OAuth2 application inside a Help Scout account (Your Profile > My apps > Create My App) and supply a redirection URL
Record the application ID and application secret
name: Help Scout
nuances: Access tokens live 2 days (expires_in 172800) in the documented token responses for both flows; expiry is signaled by HTTP 401. For client credentials: 'This token is valid for 2 days and you should create a new one only after the existing token expires.'

Token endpoint accepts JSON, form, or query params 'as long as the appropriate Content-Type header is included'. The state parameter on the authorize URL is optional and returned on the callback if used.

Plan gating is the customer's problem, not yours: 'The API is rate limited and all users associated with the same account count against the same rate limit' (write requests count as 2). Per the official help article: Standard 'Up to 200 calls per minute' (no reporting endpoints), Plus 'Up to 400 calls per minute', Pro 'Up to 800 calls per minute', and 'The Free plan does not include access to the API or integrations.'

Help Scout's official PHP client README references a legacy_token auth type that exchanges a legacy clientId and apiKey for an access token via a 'transition service': legacy API-key-era credentials are a deprecated path being migrated to OAuth2, not a current onboarding option.
Help Scout's developer home also lists sidebar 'Apps' (displaying your own content as an internal sidebar application in the Inbox), a UI embedding surface distinct from the Inbox API OAuth program.
prerequisites: A Help Scout account to create the application in
A redirection URL for the Authorization Code flow (a placeholder such as https://www.google.com is explicitly permitted for client-credentials-only apps)

steps.detail: Your Profile > My apps > Create My App. A redirection URL is necessary for the Authorization Code flow. Record the application ID and application secret.
steps.title: Create the OAuth2 application

steps.detail: Redirect the user to secure.helpscout.net/authentication/authorizeClientApplication?client_id={application_id}&state={your_secret}. If the user is already logged in they see the Authorization screen immediately; otherwise they log in first. Help Scout redirects to your Redirection URL with a code (and optionally state).
steps.title: Redirect the user to authorize

steps.detail: POST api.helpscout.net/v2/oauth2/token with code, client_id, client_secret, grant_type=authorization_code. Response: access_token, refresh_token, token_type bearer, expires_in 172800 (2 days). Call the Inbox API with Authorization: Bearer.
steps.title: Exchange the code; call the API

steps.detail: When the access token expires (HTTP 401), POST the token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token plus client credentials. The response returns a NEW access and refresh token pair; store the replacement refresh token.
steps.title: Refresh (rotating pair)

steps.detail: Read the brand guidelines on the developer home and let Help Scout know ('be sure to let us know so we can tell everyone about it'). No submission or approval stands in the way.
steps.title: Launch publicly (brand guidelines + notify)

tagline: A conventional OAuth 2.0 program (authorization code for third parties, client credentials for internal use) with 2-day access tokens and rotating refresh tokens, and, unusually, no documented review, listing approval, cap, or fee before going public.

time.active: ~5 min of app creation + ~1 hr of flow code
time.total: Same day; no review exists to wait for
